column2: the ancestor shrine deep in the hold, where the stone faces of your forefathers watch from the walls
the mortuary temple of the necropolis, among the tombs of your forefathers
the blood-dark grove where the skulls of the fathers hang from the branches
the ring of standing stones where your forefathers were laid in their barrows
the shrine in the holy grove where your forefathers are remembered
runepriest
[Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]
You have decided to go to [Root.GetOfferingPlace] and make an offering in honour of your forefathers, hoping for their aid in return. What will you ask of them?
A long and healthy life.
Affection and companionship.
Guide my arm in battle and let me crush my enemies!
Prosperity and growth for my realm.
Forefathers, share your wisdom with me!
I ask nothing. I came only to honour them.
You have asked your forefathers for health and a long life. Now it is time to make your offering. What will you give them in return?
You have asked your forefathers for aid with those close to you. Now it is time to make your offering. What will you give them in return?
You have asked your forefathers for strength and victory in battle. Now it is time to make your offering. What will you give them in return?
You have asked your forefathers for prosperity and wealth for your realm. Now it is time to make your offering. What will you give them in return?
You have asked your forefathers for guidance and knowledge. Now it is time to make your offering. What will you give them in return?
Forefathers, I offer you my own flesh and blood!
You offer your forefathers a part of your own body.\n
May this soul serve you well in the halls of the dead!
You offer your forefathers the life of one of your prisoners.\n
May this soul serve you well in the halls of the dead!
Your dungeon is empty. You offer your forefathers the life of one of your courtiers.\n
Let the gold of my house fill the ancestor hoard!
You offer your forefathers a great hoard of gold, to be sealed in the shrine for ever.\n
Forefathers, may this feast please you!
You offer your forefathers the best food and drink money can buy.\n
I had this idol carved in your honour. I hope it pleases you.
You offer your forefathers a small carving.\n

You lie down on the offering stone and brace yourself for the rite. Thankfully the [Root.GetOfferingPriest]'s knife is sharp, and soon the stone is dark with your blood. Your screams will surely have pleased your forefathers. Now all you can do is wait, and hope.

The offering struggled when the [Root.GetOfferingPriest] and the acolytes forced it down on the offering stone. Your forefathers will surely be pleased with such a vigorous servant. Now all you can do is wait, and hope.

Chest after chest of gold was carried down into the shrine and sealed behind a rune-carved stone, as the [Root.GetOfferingPriest] chanted the names of your forefathers back to the founding of the hold. A dawi gives nothing more precious. Now all you can do is wait, and hope.

Together with the [Root.GetOfferingPriest] and the acolytes you laid a great bounty of food and drink on the offering stone. You spent the whole night feasting and singing the old chants in honour of your forefathers. Now all you can do is wait, and hope.
You placed the little carved idol on the offering stone and paid your respects to your forefathers. Now all you can do is wait, and hope.
May my forefathers bestow their blessing upon me.
It is impossible to prove, but I feel better than I have in years. There is a spring in my step and my mind is clear. I am sure my forefathers are with me, keeping me strong and safe!
Forefathers, I thank you for your blessing!

I am sick, I know I am. Yet my physician is struck dumb by how much strength I have in the face of the sickness, and of late the sickness itself seems to be leaving me. I want to say my forefathers stand beside me, but I am not sure anyone would believe it.
Perhaps it is my good spirits?
I am not sure strength runs in my family, but it never hurts to try. My subjects raise their eyebrows when they see me lifting barrels and boulders for the fun of it. I feel inspired!
I would like to see my grand[Root.GetFatherMother] do push-ups on one hand like this!
It could be the nettle soup I have taken to, or the good weather, but I feel invigorated. Today someone told me I look years younger! Is this the work of my forefathers?
I feel amazing!
Ever since I begged my forefathers to mend my failing health I have felt... off. More off than usual, that is. Perhaps I asked too much of them, and gave too little.
I hope it is only my imagination...

Of late I feel I understand my people as never before. What drives them, what draws them and what repels them, it all seems so clear. And I am not imagining it, for I am met with more respect than ever.
Perhaps my forefathers are guiding me?

I do not know why I never noticed [offering_lover.GetTitledFirstName] before. In fact I remember finding [offering_lover.GetHerHim] rather plain! Yet now I find myself drawn to [offering_lover.GetHerHis] side. Perhaps my forefathers have steered me there.
I ache to confess my love to [offering_lover.GetHerHim]!
I am still not sure we are right for each other...

There are few things I enjoy more than the company of [offering_friend.GetTitledFirstName]. We were not always this close, but it is hard to remember a time when we were not. In times like these a trusted friend is a rare thing.
May our descendants be the best of allies too!
Although the way [offering_friend.GetSheHe] chews with an open mouth is really annoying.
I have thought much about my forefathers of late, and about how hard friendship is to keep. I try to be myself, but it is not always easy to get along with people. I want to make an effort.
Listening is half of every friendship.

Of late a handsome black and white cat follows me everywhere. It seems to have decided I am its [Root.GetMasterMistress]! I did ask my forefathers for companionship, though this is not quite what I had in mind.
But it is so sweet. Come here, kitty!
Shoo! Go away!

Did [offering_friend.GetTitledFirstName] always irritate me like this? Not only does [offering_friend.GetSheHe] keep interrupting me, but when we pass each other [offering_friend.GetSheHe] no longer even greets me, and I am the [Root.GetTitle]! Is this how my forefathers repay so mean an offering?
The nerve of that [offering_friend.GetManWoman]!

One of my warriors has caught my eye. [offering_commander.GetFirstName] is something else: [offering_commander.GetSheHe] beats fighters with twice [offering_commander.GetHerHis] experience in the practice yard as a matter of course. Perhaps I can find [offering_commander.GetHerHim] a better place?
Perhaps my forefathers sent [offering_commander.GetHerHim] to me?

If my forefathers taught me anything, it is that a warrior's greatness is not measured only by the strength of [Root.GetHerHis] arm or [Root.GetHerHis] skill with a weapon. To master a battlefield one must read the flow of the fight and know how to lead.
I can almost feel my forefathers guiding my hand.

Curse [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName]! Today I made a stupid mistake in the practice yard, and it cost me dearly. My opponent was not ready, and the blade went straight through my armour. Have my forefathers taken back their protection?
I will never be the same again.

My [Root.GetMarshalName] [offering_marshal.GetFirstName] has proposed some interesting changes to how we train and arm our warriors. [offering_marshal.GetSheHeCap] says the ideas came in a flash of inspiration. I am sure we have my forefathers to thank!
One of my captains has proposed some interesting changes to how we train and arm our warriors. The ideas came in a flash of inspiration, they say. I am sure we have my forefathers to thank!
Let us give these ideas a try!
Word of my offering has spread far and wide, and warriors are flocking to my banner in search of the glory of old. Together we will honour my forefathers on the battlefield!
Strength to [Root.Realm.GetName]!

The last seasons have treated my capital [Root.Capital.GetName] well. Excellently, in fact! Trade flourishes and even most of the peasants seem fed and content. I take some credit for it, but I am sure my forefathers have been watching over us.
Plague and war ravaged my capital [Root.Capital.GetName] and its people, but these last months things are mending, if my ledgers can be believed. I am certain I have my forefathers to thank.
Blessed be my forefathers!

My [Root.GetTreasurerName] [offering_treasurer.GetFirstName] has come to me with new ideas about trade and roads, all of them promising. [offering_treasurer.GetSheHeCap] says they came in a flash of inspiration. I am sure we have my forefathers to thank!
One of my advisors has come to me with new ideas about trade and roads, all of them promising. They came in a flash of inspiration, I am told. I am sure we have my forefathers to thank!
Put the plans into motion!

Of late I have struck one good bargain after another. First some fine pelts and a new blade, and today I helped my [Root.GetTreasurerName] strike an excellent deal for provisions for the army. Could my forefathers be guiding me?
I know a good deal when I see one!

One of my subjects has worked out that I have been overtaxing everyone for years, and now everyone knows it. It was an honest mistake, but they refuse to pay what they owe, claiming the difference is already paid. My forefathers were not pleased with so mean an offering, it seems.
Those stingy wretches!
I have been pondering the tales of my forefathers, and I am more than a little impressed by their wit. I think I have picked up a thing or two. They truly are a great source of knowledge.
We can always learn from those who came before.

An intriguing woman named [offering_sage.GetFirstName] has joined my court. I could tell from the first moment that she was learned, and she keeps impressing me with her knowledge and sound reasoning. Her counsel is always welcome, however harsh, and she is rarely wrong.

A wise woman named [offering_sage.GetFirstName] has joined my court. In the lands of the Ungol such hags are feared and hated, but they know the spirits of the land and the old curses, and they can smell the taint of Chaos. As the old Ungol saying goes: "Only one thing is worse than a stanitsa with a hag, and that is a stanitsa without one."

A seeress named [offering_sage.GetFirstName] has come to my hall out of the snows. She reads the bones and the blood, and the gods speak through her when the fire burns low. My warriors make the sign against her when she passes, but none of them would dare cross her.

An old loremaster named [offering_sage.GetFirstName] has come to my hold from a distant karak. He knows the Book of Grudges and the deeds of every king back to the founding of the hold, and he reckons the ancestors' wishes the way a smith reckons a weight of iron. His counsel is blunt, and always right.
A wise elder named [offering_sage.GetFirstName] has joined my court. He knows the old rites and the old tales better than any priest, and his counsel is always welcome, however harsh.
My forefathers sent this one to me.
I come into my study to find a striking owl perched on the window ledge. It watches me with piercing yellow eyes for a while, then taps the glass with its beak. Did my forefathers send it to me?
Who is a pretty bird?
Shoo, you pest! Leave me be!
My forefathers always prized a sharp mind, so I have given more time to study. Today I was out walking, pondering the mysteries of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], when a new insight struck me.
How did I never think of that before?

For weeks I have studied the tales of my forefathers with one of the elders. The old one keeps asking me about the meanings behind the stories, and my answers never seem to impress. So mean an offering earns little wisdom, it seems.
I do not think I have a mind for this...

Since the offering I have dreamed every night of my forefathers, standing in a wind that blows from no direction and from all of them at once. Now I feel that wind when I am awake. Candles gutter when I am angry, and the hounds will not meet my eyes. The Winds of Magic have found me.
Then I will learn to master them.

No one can explain it, but the sickness that has tormented me these last weeks has left my body! Every sign of it is gone and I feel as healthy as ever. By [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], it is a miracle!
Praise [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] and my forefathers!
Idol of the Forefathers
A small idol of the forefathers, its features worn smooth by the hands of generations. It was found on the offering stone the morning after a great offering, and no one remembers carving it.
